title: Finite Q3 Euclidean OS reflection Gram and thermal KMS bridge
question: For the actual finite d=3 Q3 Hamiltonians on the registered bond2, square4 and grid2x3 controls, do Euclidean transfer words give a positive OS reflection Gram on the half-period and satisfy the finite thermal cyclic/KMS word identity for every source site?

model.observables: A_x=exp(i a q_x/hbar), B_x=exp(i a p_x/hbar) for every site x

adversarial_review.check: All transfer exponents use T(s)=exp(-sH/hbar), the period beta*hbar and half-period reflection; no real-time sign is silently reused.
The positive statement is the finite transfer-word Gram identity G_ij=Tr(F_i^*F_j)/Z; it is not asserted as an infinite-volume OS reconstruction.
The direct reflected trace formula is compared entrywise with the Hilbert-Schmidt Gram construction for every source and beta.
The W_AB(s)=W_BA(beta*hbar-s) relation is checked by two separately ordered finite transfer words, not by assuming commutativity of A and B.
Only d=3 and the explicit bond2, square4 and grid2x3 finite controls are covered; no torus limit or arbitrary graph class is inferred.
Every finite source site is included, but finite Gram positivity and cyclicity do not supply a source/volume/cutoff-uniform common core or Cauchy rate.
The independent lane reconstructs oscillator tensors, Q3 terms, spectral transfer factors and Gram/cyclicity rows without importing primary code.
Lean R247 checks exact rational finite Gibbs normalization/commutation and conditional transfer scope; dense Euclidean Q3 matrices remain Python evidence.

Finite OS Gram positivity and thermal cyclicity do not identify the Hamiltonian limit with an OS mixture, construct one common alpha, prove a GNS gap, remove the cutoff, or close C6, Sector A or Pre-A.

lean_crosscheck.role: R247 checks exact rational finite Gibbs normalization/commutation; Python checks Euclidean transfer Gram positivity and thermal cyclicity for actual Q3 matrices.

qft_interface.closed: At finite volume, every declared source yields a positive semidefinite half-period transfer-word Gram and the finite thermal two-word cyclic/KMS identity is reproduced for the manifest beta/time grids.
qft_interface.open: A common-word exhaustion-compatible embedding into one OS carrier, direct D/delta-D Cauchy, common core, source/volume/beta uniformity, one common alpha, Hamiltonian-to-OS identification, GNS gap, continuum and physical TECT gates remain open.
qft_interface.tect_boundary: Auxiliary C6/Q3 finite evidence only; no heat_root_incidence, canonical A1/R-192 production owner, physical-empty reference, Sector-A closure or Pre-A closure is supplied.

next_action: Use the finite OS Gram and thermal cyclicity identities as the exact input for an exhaustion-compatible common-word map; target a source/volume-uniform two-sided seminorm Cauchy estimate, and record any failure before claiming Hamiltonian-to-OS identification.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite d=3 Euclidean transfer diagnostic. It is not an OS reconstruction theorem, thermodynamic limit, common-alpha construction, mass-gap proof, continuum result, or QFT/Clay closure.
no_overclaim: This package proves only finite matrix transfer-word positivity and cyclicity. It does not prove a thermodynamic OS measure, Hamiltonian-to-OS identification, a source-uniform common alpha, a GNS mass gap, continuum removal, C6, Sector A, Pre-A or a Clay result.
